title: Synthetic canary simulator and threshold calibrator for SLO-driven rollbacks
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Summary: Build a deterministic synthetic canary simulator and threshold calibrator that: 1) replays production-like traffic mixes (latency distributions, token cost profiles, error modes, throughput bursts) against candidate model variants; 2) runs Monte Carlo and worst-case stress sweeps to estimate false-positive/false-negative rates for rollback triggers based on latency, error-rate, token-cost-per-request, and throughput degradation; and 3) recommends calibrated SLO thresholds (and hysteresis windows) per-customer cohort and per-route to minimize unnecessary rollbacks while preserving safety.

Why: Current rollout gates use static thresholds tuned from historical runs and ad-hoc heuristics. We see noisy rollbacks during traffic spikes and false negatives when regressions are correlated with rare long-tail requests. A simulator + calibrator lets us understand sensitivity across signal mixes, set cohort-specific thresholds, and run offline experiments before pushing to canaries.

Goals:
- Deliver a repeatable simulator harness that ingests sampled traces and synthetic generators and runs batches of simulated rollouts.
- Produce a calibration report that outputs recommended thresholds for latency p95/p99, error-rate delta, token-cost-per-request increase, and throughput drop, with explicit FP/FN tradeoff curves.
- Integrate recommendations into the rollout orchestration UI as non-blocking suggestions and into the canary policy API as optional auto-tune mode.

Technical approach:
- Trace ingestion: extend the existing trace exporter to produce lightweight sampled request records (route, cohort, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_ms, status_code, baseline_model_id).
- Traffic synthesis: implement generative traffic templates (steady-state mix, bursty tail-heavy mix, and adversarial single-request storm) parameterized by sequence length distribution and route.
- Metric simulation: emulate runtime behaviors (KV cache hit/miss patterns, batching latencies, kernel selection variability) using a parametric latency model derived from recent benchmarks.
- Statistical engine: run Monte Carlo ensembles and compute operating characteristic curves for candidate rollback rules (thresholds and windows). Use bootstrap resampling to estimate confidence intervals.
- Output: JSON calibration reports, visualizable plots for the Console, and a policy patch suggestion API endpoint (draft).

Non-goals: automated enforcement of recommendations (we only propose thresholds in this ticket), and full audit-ready reports for compliance (follow-up).
acceptance_criteria: Simulator can replay a sampled day of production traces with <20% wall-time overhead compared to real-time replay on test infra.
Calibration job produces threshold recommendations (latency p95/p99, error-rate delta, token-cost increase, throughput drop) with 95% CI and an FP/FN tradeoff curve.
Console shows a mockup panel that visualizes the calibration curve and allows a user to export suggested thresholds into a canary policy JSON.
A non-blocking API endpoint returns a policy suggestion payload for use by rollout orchestrator (schema validated).
Runbook section added: how to interpret calibration reports, when to accept auto-tune suggestions, and manual override guidance.

implementation_plan: Week 1: trace exporter extension + minimal simulator that replays sampled traces.
Week 2: implement parametric latency and token-cost models; run Monte Carlo experiments on small ensembles.
Week 3: calibration report generation, CI integration, and basic Console visualization prototype.
Week 4: run cross-team validation (SRE/RE/PM) on 3 historical incidents to validate suggested thresholds.
Week 5: polish API, documentation, and rollout of feature flag behind 'sim_canary_calibrator'.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Calibration overfits to sampled traces -> Mitigation: include adversarial and burst templates and holdout validation folds.
Risk: Simulator runtime cost could be high on large ensembles -> Mitigation: implement stratified sampling and early-stop when confidence bounds are tight.
Risk: False confidence from synthetic models (misses kernel-level nondeterminism) -> Mitigation: incorporate noise models derived from per-kernel jitter histograms.
Risk: PII leakage in traces -> Mitigation: redaction pipeline and enforce sampling + privacy checks before ingestion.
